title: Plotlab — CSV Chart Workbench
description: Paste any CSV, map columns to six chart types, tune the encoding, then export SVG, 2× PNG or a share link.
concept: Plotlab is a tiny charting studio that runs entirely in the tab. Drop in a CSV or TSV — the delimiter and every column type are sniffed for you — then bind columns to X, value and series, pick an aggregate, and read the result as a bar, line, area, scatter, donut or heatmap. Every chart is drawn as real SVG, so the export is a vector file, not a screenshot. The palettes are not eyeballed: each ordering was run through a colour-vision-deficiency validator for lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair separation and surface contrast in both light and dark mode before it was offered.
features: Six chart types — bar (grouped/stacked), line, stacked area, scatter, donut and heatmap
CSV/TSV parser with quoted-field support, delimiter sniffing and number/date/text type inference
Live encoding panel: X, value, series, aggregate (sum/mean/count/max/min), ordering and a category cap
Three CVD-validated palettes, light/dark themes, smoothing, grid, value labels and clickable legend filtering
Crosshair tooltips, series folding into “Other”, four built-in sample datasets and file loading
Export vector SVG, 2× PNG, the aggregated CSV, or a shareable URL that carries the data and settings

interaction.mouse: Hover the plot for a crosshair and value tooltip; click a legend chip to hide or show a series.
interaction.click: Switch chart type, rebind columns, toggle stacking/smoothing/labels, and hit SVG, PNG or Share to take the chart with you.
interaction.touch: Tap the Data / Chart / Style tabs to move between panels; tap anywhere on the plot to read values.
interaction.keyboard: 1–6 pick a chart type, T flips the theme, G toggles the grid, S copies a share link, P exports PNG.
